title: Remove 'PositiveSentiment' and 'A_GRADE setup' from signal scoring — undefined signals
analysis: 4 of the 5 executed/attempted BUY entries included 'PositiveSentiment' as a fired signal (NVDA 2026-05-15, AAPL 2026-05-18, META x4 on 2026-05-19, AMD 2026-05-20). One AAPL entry included 'A_GRADE setup'. Neither 'PositiveSentiment' nor 'A_GRADE setup' appears anywhere in CLAUDE.md's signal scoring table. These are LLM-invented signals that are contributing to score inflation — a trade scoring 3 valid points plus 1 invented 'PositiveSentiment' point appears to pass the 2-signal threshold when it may only have 1-2 valid signals. The META entries on 2026-05-19 show RSI<45 + BelowMA20>1% + ADX<25 + PositiveSentiment = score 4, but if PositiveSentiment is excluded, the valid score is RSI<45(+1) + BelowMA20(+1) + ADX<25(+1) = 3 — still valid. However for NVDA and AMD, removing undefined signals from momentum entries would drop them below threshold.
rationale: Undefined signals that pad scores create inconsistent entry quality. 'PositiveSentiment' appearing in 80% of attempted entries suggests the LLM is using it as a default filler. Since there is no sentiment data feed defined in the system, this signal cannot be reliably or consistently measured, and its inclusion is arbitrary.

insight.why_now: 'PositiveSentiment' appeared in 4/5 actionable journal entries and 'A_GRADE setup' in 1. These signals do not exist in CLAUDE.md. Their consistent appearance suggests the LLM is hallucinating confirmatory signals to justify trades it wants to take.
insight.purpose: Enforce signal purity — only the 5 CLAUDE.md-defined signals can contribute to score. This prevents score inflation from invented signals and makes the threshold requirement meaningful.
insight.expected_effect: Trades with inflated scores due to 'PositiveSentiment' will either still pass on legitimate signals alone, or correctly fail the threshold. Eliminates a source of false confidence in signal scoring.
insight.risks: If many borderline trades relied on PositiveSentiment to reach threshold=2, frequency may drop further. However given the primary issue is the bot trading wrong-direction signals entirely, this is a secondary concern.

current_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING (need 2+ to enter under medium_safety profile)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +1 point
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)
proposed_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING (need 2+ to enter under medium_safety profile)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +1 point
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)

CRITICAL: ONLY these 5 signals exist. Do NOT invent signals such as 'PositiveSentiment', 'A_GRADE setup', 'RSI>65 (strong momentum)', 'AboveMA20>1%', or any other signal not listed above. If you find yourself firing a signal not in this list, that signal scores 0 points and must NOT appear in signals_fired. Fabricated signals that inflate score to meet threshold = immediate SKIP.

title: Max positions = 3 is blocking all new entries for 30+ consecutive cycles
analysis: From 2026-05-15 through 2026-05-20, open_positions=3 appears in 38 of 50 journal entries. During this period, the bot SKIPped or REJECTED every potential entry. The 4 META BUY attempts on 2026-05-19 (signal_score=4, R:R=3.10-3.36) were all REJECTED because META was already held. The AAPL BUY on 2026-05-20 (signal_score=4, R:R=2.36) was REJECTED because AAPL was already held. The bot appears to be permanently parked at max capacity (3 positions) with no exits occurring during the observed window, meaning the position management/exit logic is not functioning. Account value drifted from $98,502 to $98,649 over the full period — essentially flat with no completed trade cycles visible.
rationale: If positions are never exiting (no closed trade outcomes visible in 50 entries), the time stop rule (exit after 3 days) should be triggering but there is no evidence of it. The bot is in a deadlock: holding 3 positions indefinitely, generating valid signals, then REJECTing them due to position conflicts. The 3-day time stop must be enforced aggressively, and the max positions rule may need a companion rule forcing oldest-position review when at capacity.

insight.why_now: 38/50 entries show open_positions=3 with zero exits observed. Four high-quality META signals (R:R > 3.0) and one AAPL signal were wasted due to position conflicts. This represents the single largest source of opportunity cost in the journal.
insight.purpose: Ensure the time stop exit rule is actually executing. Add an explicit check: if open_positions >= MAX and a new signal scores 4+, force a review of all open positions for time stop eligibility before SKIPping.
insight.expected_effect: Restores trade throughput. Allows the bot to cycle through setups instead of being perpetually blocked. Captures high-R:R setups like the META series that are currently being wasted.
insight.risks: Forcing exits to free capacity could close positions at suboptimal times. The time stop at 3 days is a rule for a reason — enforcing it harder is correct, but the underlying positions may be underwater when forced out.

current_rule: - Time stop: Exit any position open longer than 3 days regardless of P&L
proposed_rule:
- Time stop: Exit any position open longer than 3 days regardless of P&L. This rule is NON-NEGOTIABLE and must be checked at the START of every cycle before evaluating new entries.
- Capacity check: If open_positions >= 3 (max) AND a new signal scores 4+, immediately audit all open positions for time stop eligibility BEFORE issuing SKIP or REJECT. If any position has been held 3+ days, exit it first, then evaluate the new entry.
- Log every time stop exit explicitly with action='SELL', rejection_reason='TIME_STOP_3DAY_FORCED'.
